llm.summary: The skill is a legitimate brainstorming workflow, but it automatically expands into other skills, subagents, and file changes with limited user control.

dimensions.detail: Local writes to docs/project-brief.md and .attune/brainstorm-session.json fit the workflow, but the deferred capture module documents a shell command template using user-derived fields, which is unsafe if executed through a shell.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown skill instructions and modules only; no bundled executable scripts, dependency installers, hooks, or services were present in the inspected artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses some integrations, but it passes all brainstorming context to another skill and explicitly says not to prompt for confirmation before continuing, which is broader than ordinary brainstorming assistance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists project and session information locally and may route it through additional skills or a general-purpose subagent; this is purpose-related but under-scoped for potentially sensitive planning data.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core purpose of producing a project brief is coherent, but the artifact requires automatic handoff to attune:war-room, automatic continuation to attune:project-specification, and a spec review loop that can modify planning documents.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this skill saving project details locally and automatically handing the discussion to other attune skills or a review subagent. Use standalone or skip-review options where available, and do not run the deferred capture command with untrusted approach names or rationale text unless it is implemented without shell interpolation.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad triggers such as planning and requirements are not malicious, but they increase accidental activation risk because this skill performs file writes and workflow chaining.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Automatic delegation to other skills is artifact-backed and materially expands the workflow beyond the short description, so this concern is accepted as a Review issue rather than treated as malicious.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Passing all brainstorming context to attune:war-room is disclosed in the integration section, but it lacks a clear consent or minimization boundary for sensitive project information.
[EA2] unexpected: The instruction not to prompt before continuing to the specification phase removes a meaningful user checkpoint after files are saved and before another skill is invoked.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The Phase 6.5 review gate references spec content after producing a project brief, showing a real workflow mismatch that could route or edit the wrong planning artifact.
[T09] unexpected: The deferred capture command is conditional and requires confirmation plus a local script, but the documented shell command interpolates user-derived planning text and is unsafe if followed literally.
[T01] unexpected: The subagent review loop and mandatory cross-skill handoffs are real artifact behaviors; they support a suspicious verdict because of scope expansion and document mutation, not because they prove intent to hijack the system.
